summary: Toshio Nagahiro was a scholar of history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He served at Kyoto University, its Institute for Research in Humanities, Kurokawa Institute of Ancient Cultures, and was president of Kyoto Tachibana University.

Toshio Sako specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and Yasunori Ejima, and at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

Toshio Yamazaki was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1977), Chuo University (~1977–1987), Tokyo Institute of Technology, and Hannan University.

Toshiya Unebe works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Having studied under Musashi Tachikawa, he served as an associate professor in Indian Studies at Nagoya University (attested 2006–2011).

Totsudo Kato worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Oriental Hall, Kyoto Horitsu Gakko, and Chuo University under teachers including Seiran Ouchi, Enryo Inoue, and Bankon Shimada, later teaching at Shakutoku Kyoko, Setagaya Gakuen, Komazawa, Toyo, and Nihon universities.

Touhoi Fok was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies, Otani University, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, where he also lectured from around 1972 to 1988.

Touraj Daryaee is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, history, and archaeology fields. He studied at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1993–1999) and held a post at the University of California, Irvine (~2007).

Towao Sakaehara is a historian and Japanologist who earned his doctorate at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Otemon Gakuin University, served as professor at Osaka City University, and was director of the Osaka Museum of History (2014–2020).
Traian Costa was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Vlad Bănățeanu. He served as a professor at the University of Bucharest, where he taught Sanskrit in 1963.

Trang T. D. Nguyen works in Buddhist and religious studies, with degrees from Ho Chi Minh City Open University and University of South Wales, and doctoral study at the University of Vienna. Nguyen held posts at organizations including Play for Peace.

Travis L. Smith is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at UC Berkeley and Columbia University (PhD 2007). He studied under John Stratton Hawley and others, later teaching at Barnard College, University of Florida, and UC Berkeley.
Trent Walker works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Alexander von Rospatt.

Trevor Leggett worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology, studying at King's College London, SOAS, and under teachers including Hari Prasad Shastri and Arthur Waley. He headed the BBC Japanese Service (~1946–1970) and lectured for the Buddhist Society.

Trevor Ling was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford. He taught theology and comparative religion, holding posts at Nottingham, Rangoon, Leeds (1963–1972), Manchester (1972–1982), and Visva-Bharati University.

Trijang Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar who studied at Gyuto Monastery and under teachers including Pabongka Dechen Nyingpo. He succeeded Ling Rinpoche and taught prominent figures including the 14th Dalai Lama, Kelsang Gyatso, and Geshe Rabten.

Trine Brox specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at UiT and the University of Copenhagen under MA supervisor Christian K. Wedemeyer, and later became an instructor and associate professor at the University of Copenhagen.
Trinle Lhundrub studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Tro Shul Khenpo Jampal Dorjé studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Troy Organ was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa (~1939–1941). He held academic posts at Parsons College, the University of Akron, Chatham University, and Ohio University.

Trulshik Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar who studied under teachers such as Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche. He taught numerous students, including the 14th Dalai Lama, Phakchok Rinpoche, and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.
